# Brad Burch

> Senior full-stack and product engineer in San Francisco, open to the Midwest. 8 years across Salesforce, Total Brain, Front, and Pawservation. Designs, builds, and runs Claude agents, MCP servers with OAuth 2.1 + PKCE, and Stripe Connect payments in TypeScript, Python, and PostgreSQL.

Looking for senior Software Engineer, Full Stack, or Product Engineer roles (selectively Forward Deployed and AI Engineer) at Series B or later companies. San Francisco, or relocating to Chicago, Minneapolis-St. Paul, Detroit, Columbus, Indianapolis, or Ann Arbor. US citizen, no sponsorship required.

## Selected work

- Pawservation booking platform: the multi-tenant, productized version of Brad Paws, the San Francisco pet-care business it grew out of. Stripe Connect payments, 30+ active clients, 60+ bookings a month. Auto-charge happens at most once per stay (a database uniqueness claim before Stripe is called, tested with 20 concurrent writers). Removed the source of 97% of daily database writes.
- Brad Paws client portal: serverless React 19 + Hono portal that replaced 5 to 15 hours a month of manual invoicing, reconciliation, and scheduling. Cut CPU per invoice PDF from 154 ms to 18 ms, recovering 4 months of failed invoice runs.
- Claude booking agent: human approval on every write (95% approved as submitted), 98% of 1,249 eval cases passing every run (97% on untuned Sonnet), 0 unapproved writes in 5,418 eval turns, about 8x lower per-turn model cost.
- MCP server with a hand-built OAuth 2.1 + PKCE authorization server, stateless on serverless infrastructure.
- MCP Auth Kit (open source): OAuth 2.1 + PKCE, rate limiting, scope-gated tools, two-phase confirmation.
- Roadrunner (open source): Python/Django and PostgreSQL app matching eBird and iNaturalist observations to Strava activities.
